patterns.pattern: Users have access to content and actions based on their assigned roles or permissions.
patterns.example_phrasing: Permissions are determined by a user's role (admin, editor, viewer, etc.)

patterns.pattern: Content (e.g., pages, posts, datasets) can be set as public or restricted; access may be limited to specific user types, groups, or those with passwords.
patterns.example_phrasing: Pages can be restricted to logged-in users, groups, or password-protected.

patterns.pattern: Content, objects, or files can be assigned to multiple collections and collections can contain other collections or items.
patterns.example_phrasing: Items can be members of multiple collections, and collections may nest or aggregate items/other collections.

patterns.pattern: Major data actions (creation, updates, deletions, imports, exports) must be tracked for audit purposes.
patterns.example_phrasing: Track all events and changes on collections, objects, and files.

patterns.pattern: There are configurable privacy or visibility settings per content/page type or per dataset, adjustable by authorized users.
patterns.example_phrasing: Visibility of datasets and pages can be set to public or hidden at any time.

patterns.pattern: Authentication is required for certain sensitive actions or areas, supporting multiple methods (e.g., LDAP, local accounts).
patterns.example_phrasing: Users authenticate using LDAP or local credentials to access restricted features.

patterns.pattern: Custom metadata fields can be attached to content items by authorized roles (e.g., staff, administrators, curators).
patterns.example_phrasing: Staff can add custom metadata fields to items as needed.

patterns.pattern: Bulk operations (upload, import, export) are supported, subject to role-based permission checks.
patterns.example_phrasing: Bulk upload and import/export actions can be performed by certain roles with proper permissions.

patterns.pattern: Content lifecycles and access can be governed by publication status, embargo periods, or versioning controls.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only published content is public; embargoed items remain hidden until release.

patterns.pattern: Administrators (or designated superusers) can manage all system content, settings, and user permissions.
patterns.example_phrasing: Administrators may view and manage all content and user accounts.

patterns.pattern: Each piece of content (e.g., blog post, page) belongs to at least one organizational container (section, collection, repository, etc.), and organizational containers are configurable per site/app.
patterns.example_phrasing: A blog post is assigned to a section or collection; containers can be independently configured.

patterns.pattern: Site templates and user interface elements support customization for look, feel, forms, and accessibility requirements.
patterns.example_phrasing: Templates and forms are configurable for branding and accessibility (e.g., login, password-required pages).

patterns.pattern: Editors must ensure accessibility compliance (e.g., provide alt text for images, avoid empty headings).
patterns.example_phrasing: Editors supply alt text or flag images as decorative, and should not leave headings blank.

patterns.pattern: Legal and rights information (licenses, rights statements) can be assigned at various levels (collection, object, file).
patterns.example_phrasing: Assign rights or licenses at collection or individual item level.

patterns.pattern: Taxonomies/tags for organizing content are flat (not nested) and can be used for content aggregation and filtering.
patterns.example_phrasing: Tags assigned to content are flat, enabling filtering and aggregation.

patterns.pattern: URLs are human-friendly/prettified by default, and site structure determines URL and template selection.
patterns.example_phrasing: Section names form URL paths; pretty URLs are used.

patterns.pattern: Embargoes and access locks can prevent content from being visible/available until specified conditions/dates are met.
patterns.example_phrasing: Access may be embargoed until a certain date or condition is satisfied.

patterns.pattern: Published/deleted status of content is reflected immediately to visitors/users as appropriate.
patterns.example_phrasing: Deleted posts are removed instantly; only published items are shown.

patterns.pattern: All data validations (field length, allowed values, uniqueness, etc.) follow schema or external rules.
patterns.example_phrasing: Field values must conform to schema or integration-specific requirements.

patterns.pattern: Platform supports multiple language/translations for content, establishing links between translated pages.
patterns.example_phrasing: Pages with matching translation keys are linked as alternate-language versions.
